newsitem.title: USA: Higher US rate fears spur steady corp debt supply.
newsitem.headline: Higher US rate fears spur steady corp debt supply.

text.p: Fears of possible higher interest rates continues to trigger a steady supply of new corporate debt offerings with more seen on the horizon, dealers said.
"We've seen a number of deals come and more are in the pipeline," said one high-grade syndicate source.
"Basically, issuers are saying we're not going to below 7.0 percent, so everybody's just getting their stuff done. It's basically fear of higher interest rates," the source said.

Although business is getting done, the large amount of new supply appears to be weighing down on the market forcing some underwriters to readjust price talk on some deals, syndicate sources said. As a result, widening in spreads in some sectors of the secondary market were seen, they said.
"It's not as easy as it has been...over the last couple of weeks some underwriters have been forced to set more realistic price levels on their deals," another syndicate source said.
"We've seen corporate deals restructured," he added. "Some deals have been delayed, some 100-year issues pulled, and different covenants put on various deals."
Market sources said the underwriters for $900 million deal for Banc One Corp moved price talk to cheaper levels this morning as a result of the uncertainty in the market.
Banc One Corp's $900 million two-part debt offering, launched on Thursday, includes $400 million in 10-year debt and $500 million of a 30-year issue, dealers said.
"Long bank paper is not the most appetizing structure for some buyers," said one syndicate official.
"There is uneasiness about bank earnings with rates going up. This is just a lot of paper to get priced in this environment," he added.
He noted the large Banc One deal was causing spreads on long-term bank paper to widen in the secondary market.
Initial price talk for the 10-year issue was seen in the 70 basis points area and is now quoted at 71-73 basis points, syndicate sources said.
Price talk on the 30-year issue, initially expected between the low-to-mid 90 basis points area, is now seen at 95-97 points, they said.
Meanwhile, players said the 30-year tranche was now issue- bid on the street.
Another deal being watched is Comcast Corp unit, Comcast Cable Communications Inc's $1.0 billion multi-tranche private placement debt offering, slated to price on Thursday, sources said.
The Ba1/BBB-minus rated deal is expected to include four tranches. Unofficial price talk is seen as follows, sources said.
- $150 million in seven-year notes with price talk seen at 125-137.5 basis points over Treasuries.
- $400 million in 10-year debt with price talk seen at 150-162.5 basis points over Treasuries.
Last month, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to tighten credit, hiking the key overnight lending rate by 25 basis points.
Elsewhere, SK Telecom's $230 million yankee debt offering was restructured to include a seven-year maturity instead of an initally planned 10-year issue, market sources said.
The yankee bond's maturity was shortened due to difficult market conditions in the Korean yankee bond market, sources said.
Seperately, Tenaga Nasional, a Malaysian electric utility, decided to bump up the size of its yankee debt offering and to $800 million, from an initially expected $500 million sale, dealer said.
The deal, which initially included a 10-year noncallable issue, now includes a second 10-year tranche with a five-year put option, sources said.
UBS Securities is expected to underwrite the offering.

Still, CSX Corp is expected to issue $2.0 billion in a multi-tranche debt offering. The deal is expected to include five-year, seven-year, 10-year and 30-year tranches, in addition, to a 30-year trust preferred issue, sources said.
On Wednesday, Moody's Investors Service cut the rating of CSX Corp senior unsecured debt to Baa2 from Baa1.
Investors are likely to use the move to demand a higher yield on CSX's $2 billion debt offering expected to hit the market in several weeks, syndicate officials said.

Moody's said the action was the result of weakened debt protection measurements at CSX following financing of its share of the acquisition of Conrail as well as increased competitive pressures in Conrail's territory.
CSX has agreed to acquire 42 percent of Conrail's assets, while Norfolk Southern Corp will acquire 58 percent.
Norfolk Southern Corp is also rumored to bring a mega mult-tranche debt offering of between $3.0 - $4.0 billion, sources added.
Investment-grade issuers tapped the market with over $1 billion in new paper on Wednesday, that followed $1.2 billion in new corporate paper on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Corporations are definitely acting differently then they did over the last two years," said one high-grade dealer.
"Basically, issuers would wait out a period like this, waiting for the market to rally, for prices to go higher, before they issued, but they're not doing it this time," he said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading off 6/32 at 94-4/32 to yield 7.10 percent.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
